question: Should OpenAI device-code authentication adopt a fixed 30-second deadline for each fetch-plus-body operation, with only authorization-poll timeouts retried until the existing overall deadline?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and well proven, but this fixed deadline becomes user-visible authentication-provider policy for slow networks and proxies; repository history does not establish that exact value and retry boundary as an already approved contract.

options.title: Accept the bounded policy
options.body: Refresh onto current main and merge with the 30-second deadline, fail-fast user-code/token exchange, and retryable authorization polls.

options.title: Adjust the fixed duration
options.body: Keep the same implementation shape but select a different provider-owned constant before merging if 30 seconds is considered too aggressive.

options.title: Pause the behavior change
options.body: Leave the PR open until maintainers can validate the deadline against expected slow-network and proxy environments.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded policy
recommendation.body: Refresh onto current main and merge with the 30-second deadline, fail-fast user-code/token exchange, and retryable authorization polls.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current device-code flow and are best positioned to confirm its intended timeout and retry contract.
